title: KV sequence signature catalog and version safelist for long-context onboarding
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Produce a reproducible per-model 'sequence signature' catalog (quantile-backed descriptors of token-length, attention-span, and KV hot-prefix distributions) and a safe-listing workflow that maps signatures to pinned runtime/model-version recommendations during onboarding. This will enable deterministic KV retention policies and safe default pins for long-context evals without manual iteration by model owners.

Scope:
- Sampling and signature extraction for incoming model artifacts (both encoder-decoder and decoder-only).
- Defining a compact canonical signature schema (stringified vector of quantiles + categorical flags) so signatures can be indexed and compared.
- A permissive safelist algorithm that recommends a pinned runtime/model-variant for a given signature, with a fallback escalation path when performance delta > 15% vs baseline.
- Integration points: model-onboarding pipeline, model catalog metadata, and the profile publishing service used by infra to distribute KV retention rules.

Acceptance criteria: 
1) For 10 curated models (open and verified), extract signatures from a 100k sample of real request traces and store canonical signatures in the catalog.
2) A safelist function that returns a pinned-version recommendation string and confidence score for any new signature.
3) End-to-end test: onboarding a model with a signature close to a catalog entry auto-creates a runtime pin and publishes a KV retention profile draft to the profile store (see runbook link).
4) Docs and telemetry: produce a dashboard showing signature distance distribution and % pinned-onboarding decisions by week.

Notes on design choices and trade-offs:
- Signature compactness vs fidelity: we chose quantiles at {10,25,50,75,90,99} for prefix length and kv-kept-lifetime to balance storage and discriminative power. This keeps the signature a short CSV string rather than a heavy protobuf.
- Sampling bias: sampling from production traces introduces product skew. We will stratify by route and device to reduce bias (see sampling plan).
- Safelist conservatism: initial threshold for direct pin is distance < 0.12 (cosine on normalized quantile vector). Between 0.12 and 0.25 will create a 'candidate pin' requiring manual review and run a cheap microbench (10 warmup traces) before auto-apply.

Artifacts and links:
- Draft spec: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3k-seq-signatures (doc: "seq-signature-spec-v1")
- Sampling plan spreadsheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/seq-sampling-2026
- Onboarding runbook PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform-docs/pull/78
- Prototype code: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-tools/tree/feat/signatures (WIP)
- Dashboard prototype (internal): https://grafana.redwood.cloud/d/kv-signatures/overview

Operational concerns:
- This catalog will grow; we will TTL entries older than 180 days unless owners revalidate. TTL-controlled retention avoids stale pins.
- Edge cases: very long prefix models (>=64k tokens) may produce heavy KV lifetime tails; we will mark these with the flag 'long-tail: true' to force manual review.
- Rollout plan: start with internal-only model set (10 models) for 2 cycles, then enable auto-pin for models with confidence >=0.85.

Longer-term: integrate model architecture fingerprint (layer-count, attn-type) into signature to improve matching for novel architectures.
